Date: 2027-07-21
Start: 14:00 EDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Recording: Yes
Redwood: Ava Martinez (AE), Ethan Cho (SE)
Orchid Systems: Maya Patel (Head of ML), Jonas Keller (CTO), Priya Singh (Data Engineer), Liam O'Connor (Product Manager)
summary: Discovery call to evaluate open-model choices (Mistral, Llama, Falcon variants), discuss context length needs (32k vs 64k), multilingual support (EN/FR/JP), and tool-calling for internal search and database lookups. Customer leaning toward Dedicated for performance and data residency but wants clarity on fallback to Hosted and private VPC options. Action: share security docs, run bench, size Dedicated pool, pilot with sample prompts.
topics: Context length requirements and KV cache behavior
Multilingual performance and tokenization for Japanese/French
Tool-calling: web search + internal RDB lookups + function calling
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/KMS/HSM) tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check — audio okay?
[00:05] Maya (Orchid): Yep, good here. thanks.
[00:08] Jonas (CTO): All good.
[00:10] Ava: Perfect. quick agenda — model selection, context length, multilingual, tool-calling and ops options. Ethan will handle the deeper perf and infra questions. Sound ok?
[00:18] Liam (PM): Yep. we're especially worried about latency for search suggestions and also preserving user data residency.
[00:25] Ethan (Redwood SE): Great; we'll walk through Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and how the runtime handles long contexts and tool integration. Maya, can you describe the core use cases and languages?
[00:35] Maya: Sure. Primary is a customer support assistant — English and French right now, plan to add Japanese later. conversations average 6–8 turns but some escalations need 10–15k of context, and for the knowledge-heavy cases we'd like 32k tokens to start. We're exploring 64k for a small subset.
[00:50] Priya (Data Eng): Also we call internal RDBs to fetch account metadata, and we do fuzzy search over our docs. That needs secure tool-calling, ideally with per-request audit logs.
[01:05] Ethan: Okay, that's helpful. on context — Redwood's runtime supports models with extended context. For open models, Mistral-7B and Llama-2 variants have different tradeoffs. Mistral-7B sizes well for cost but for 32k and up, Llama-2-70B or Falcon-40B with quantization are common picks. Note: performance can vary a lot with quantization and kernel selection. (slight pause)
[01:30] Jonas: Can you give a rough latency ballpark for a 32k prompt?
[01:33] Ethan: Roughly, on Dedicated with a 1-stream per GPU config — 32k completion with a 2k output might be in the 600–900ms per-token step depending on beam/temperature. for short replies it's lower, but the big factor is memory bandwidth and KV cache hit rate. Hosted may add regional network hops. These are estimates; we'll run bench.
[01:55] Maya: When you say KV cache, is that the prefix caching? we need to keep recent convo history across sessions for continuity.
[02:02] Ethan: yes, KV cache/prefix caching — we expose controls. Redwood's autoscaler keeps warm KV caches for pinned sessions on Dedicated; on Hosted we do prefix caching but eviction policies are different. sometimes the transcription will say K-V cash in logs — it's spelled weird in old logs (laughs).
[02:20] Liam: (laughs) ok. Data residency — we need EU hosting for EU customers. Is Dedicated in EU possible?
[02:27] Ava: Absolutely. Dedicated capacity can be reserved in EU regions; Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) also available if you need full network isolation. We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key control.
[02:36] Jonas: What's the difference between Dedicated and Private from a security standpoint?
[02:39] Ethan: Dedicated means reserved GPU pools in our infra with tenant isolation and dedicated network boundaries — you don't share GPUs with other customers. Private adds a customer-managed control plane or even on-prem if needed; that gives you more control over the control plane, VPC peering, and full physical isolation if required. Both options support SSO, RBAC and audit logs.
[02:55] Priya: How do we handle KMS integrations? We use AWS KMS today but evaluating Azure Key Vault for some teams.
[03:02] Ava: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations. we can also do customer-managed keys in Private. We'll send the security pack with integration notes.
[03:10] Jonas: Nice. on models — which one would you recommend for multilingual and code-switching use cases?
[03:15] Ethan: For multilingual, Falcon and some Llama-2-variants are strong. Mistral has good instruction tuning for English; multilingual sometimes needs fine-tuning or a model that was trained with multi-lingual corpora. tokenization matters — for Japanese you might need sentencepiece-tuned models. we can help evaluate tokenization mismatch.
[03:33] Maya: We're leaning away from closed APIs because of data residency and cost of high volume. so open models + Dedicated seems right, but we want a fall-back Hosted plan in case of spikes. can Redwood do automatic fallback?
[03:44] Ava: Yes — Smart routing can route by policy. you can prefer Dedicated but failover to Hosted-compatible variants if capacity is exhausted. there's also per-request policy to force private-only for certain routes.
[03:55] Liam: Tool-calling — we need to call an internal search API and a function that retrieves sensitive account data. How are secrets handled?
[04:02] Ethan: Tool-calls run inside the runtime with encrypted transit. For sensitive lookups we recommend sending minimal PII tokens and doing the actual sensitive fetch in your VPC via a webhook; Redwood can handle signed short-lived credentials for that. Audit logs record tool invocations but the payload scrubbing is configurable.
[04:20] Priya: what's the latency penalty for tool-calls?
[04:23] Ethan: A remote webhook adds RTT; typical additional latency is 50–200ms depending on the endpoint. We support local adapter patterns to reduce RTT on Dedicated / Private.
[04:33] Jonas: Cost: any idea relative to closed APIs? open model Dedicated + quantization should be cheaper at scale?
[04:40] Ethan: Generally yes. open models on Dedicated with int8 quantization can cut per-token compute a lot. Redwood Optimize recommends batch sizes and quantization profiles per workload. We'll produce a cost model after the pilot.
[04:54] Maya: About quantization — do you see quality regressions for multilingual when moving to int8?
[04:59] Ethan: sometimes. we recommend running evals on your prompt set. Redwood has an eval harness to compare perplexity / exact-match on your data pre- and post-quant. We'll help set that up.
[05:12] Ava: quick clarification — do you have internal SLOs for latency and availability?
[05:16] Liam: We want sub-1s for interactive suggestions and 99.9% for inference.
[05:20] Ethan: 99.9% is feasible on Dedicated with appropriate redundancy. For sub-1s you'll want a Dedicated pool sized for your peak qps with regional placement.
[05:28] Maya: For the pilot, we'd like to test three models: Mistral-7B, Llama-2-70B quantized, and Falcon-40B to see tradeoffs.
[05:35] Ethan: Good set. we'll run latency and accuracy on your 200 sample conversations and 1000 synthetic queries.
[05:42] Jonas: How long would it take to set up Dedicated pilot?
[05:45] Ava: We can spin a small Dedicated pool within 2–3 business days after contract for simple cases. if you require Private VPC peering and KMS integration it can take longer — typically 2–3 weeks.
[05:55] Priya: Can we get per-request logging? and retention controls?
[05:58] Ethan: Yes. audit logs are available with retention tiers. we can redact or mask fields, and you control retention policy for PII fields.
[06:07] Liam: On canary deploys / rollouts — we push new model versions gradually?
[06:11] Ava: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies on regressions. we also support metric-guarded rollouts based on your evals.
[06:19] Maya: ok. curious about tool-calling patterns — can the model call internal SQL functions and get structured JSON back reliably?
[06:27] Ethan: yes — we support structured tool-calling and function schemas. you can enforce strict output formats or let the model freeform and run a post-parser. router will verify schema in the runtime. sometimes transcripts show function-calling spelled as function-calling or tool calling — weird ASR things.
[06:42] Jonas: any customers using Redwood for multi-region compliance?
[06:44] Ava: yes, several enterprise customers run Dedicated in EU and US and use routing policies for data residency. Private deployments are common in regulated industries.
[06:52] Liam: Are there any limitations we should be aware of for 64k contexts?
[06:56] Ethan: Memory becomes the main limitation. for 64k you might need model sharding or multiple GPUs per request which affects latency and throughput. we can recommend a model variant and quantization profile to make 64k feasible. also note batching is less effective for very long requests.
[07:16] Maya: On multilingual benchmarks — do you have LLMs that do well on Japanese?
[07:20] Ethan: Some community models have decent Japanese coverage; you might still want to fine-tune or include language-specific tokenizers. we can run the eval suite on your Japanese test corpus.
[07:30] Priya: About credentials for tool-calls — can we rotate tokens automatically?
[07:33] Ethan: yes, we support short-lived credentials and automatic rotation for webhooks; for Private you can bring your own secret management.
[07:40] Jonas: Legal/procurement — any standard terms for Dedicated pilots?
[07:43] Ava: We have pilot agreements and NDAs. for pilots with dedicated infra there's typically a small monthly pilot fee; we'll include details in the pricing template.
[07:52] Liam: This is great. can you include a simple sample architecture diagram for Hosted fallback -> Dedicated -> Private?
[07:58] Ava: yes, we'll attach a diagram and a checklist for the pilot.
[08:02] Maya: Could you also recommend metrics we should monitor during the pilot?
[08:05] Ethan: sure — latency p50/p95, token cost per request, tool-call RTT, KV cache hit rate, top failure modes and mismatch rates for tool outputs.
[08:14] Ava: ok last bit — we'll send the security pack, pricing template, bench plan. can we reconvene next Tuesday for sizing?
[08:21] Jonas: next Tuesday works. 
[08:23] Maya: works for me.
[08:25] Priya: yes.
[08:26] Ava: Awesome. Thanks everyone. we'll follow up with links.
[08:30] Liam: thanks.
[08:32] (call ends)

Notes: ASR had a few mis-typed product names in places (e.g., Mistrial -> Mistral, K-V cash -> KV cache). Shared artifacts: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack.pdf , https://redwood.example.com/pilot-pricing.xlsx , https://redwood.example.com/bench-plan.md
